candidates.summary: A deeper promoted method or field now silently wins over a shallower one when the shared visited set has already pruned the shallower type
candidates.failure_scenario: T{Sub; C}, Sub{A; W}, W{C}, with A and C each declaring M() and a field V. Go resolves T.M to C.M and T.V to C.V (depth 1). Inside Sub, the new comparison drops W.C.M as deeper, but C is still marked in the shared m, so T's own embedded C then returns nil and Sub.A.M (depth 2) is taken as the only candidate. Head prints 'iface: A / method: A / field: a' where Go prints C / C / c. go/types accepts the program, so a realm with this shape clears addpkg and every t.M(), i.M() and t.V reads or calls the wrong member with no error. Base rejected it at preprocess, because Sub's two matches returned none: the diff turns a loud rejection into a wrong call that reports success.

candidates.summary: A valid program the base accepted is now rejected: the walk no longer stops at a same-depth conflict, so it marks a type that a shallower sibling needs
candidates.failure_scenario: T{Amb; C}, Amb{A; B; W}, W{C}, with A, B and C each declaring M(). Go resolves T.M to C.M at depth 1; Amb's A/B ambiguity at depth 2 is shadowed. The deleted 'conflict detected. return none.' returned at B before W was walked, so C stayed unvisited and base resolved T.M to C.M. Head sets ambiguous and keeps walking, enters W, marks C in the shared m, and T's own embedded C then returns nil: preprocess panics 'missing field M in main.T'. go/types accepts, so this is the direction the PR set out to close: addpkg passes type-check and then fails at VM preprocess. It also refutes the PR body's 'zero-regression' claim. Inference, not run: runtime interface calls re-run the lookup with the running binary (values.go:1962-1966 panics 'method M not found in type'), so a T held in an interface by a realm deployed before the upgrade would panic on i.M() afterwards.

candidates.summary: A diamond ambiguity paired with any deeper same-named member is now accepted and runs the diamond's method, where base rejected it as Go does
candidates.failure_scenario: T{A; B; C}, A{Base}, B{Base}, C{D}, D{E}, with Base and E each declaring M(). Go: depth 2 holds Base.M twice, so the selector is ambiguous and the program does not compile. Head: B's revisit of Base is pruned and read as no match (trail2 == nil, continue), so Base.M is the only depth-2 candidate and beats E.M at depth 3; T{}.M() prints 'base'. Base saw two candidates and rejected it, as Go does. The ADR files the diamond false accept as 'unchanged from upstream'; this shape is new with the diff. On-chain go/types rejects it first, so the loss falls on gno run and any VM caller that skips type-check, which runs a program Go rejects.

candidates.summary: The internal-ambiguity fixture is rejected only because Clean embeds the same A the shared set pruned; a Clean with its own M type is accepted
candidates.failure_scenario: Change the sibling shape: type C struct{}; func (C) M() string { return "C" }; type Clean struct{ C }. Go: depth 2 holds A.M, B.M and C.M, so T.M is ambiguous and rejected. Head: Amb's walk sets ambiguous and returns nil, which carries no depth, so at T the check trail == nil admits Clean's C.M as the only candidate; T implements I and i.M() runs C.M. The fixture and the ADR say it guards 'an internally-ambiguous sibling alongside a clean one', but it only pins the dedup of A: the shared-set prune makes Clean return nil. Base accepts the same variant, so the defect predates the diff; the gap is that the test credited to the rule pins nothing of it.
